source_evidence: Variable annuities allow you, during the accumulation phase, to direct your contributions to a menu of different mutual funds.
answer: A variable annuity is a deferred annuity in which, during the accumulation phase, you choose among investment options such as mutual funds. Its return depends on how the selected funds perform, so gains and losses are not limited. Variable annuities also have explicit fees under the contract and fees charged by the underlying mutual funds. Review the contract’s risks, costs, and features before considering one.
